name: 1 Division (Kaduna)
summary: Headquarters in Kaduna; northwest core states (Kaduna, Kano, Jigawa, Katsina).
description: The 1 Division is one of the Nigerian Army's oldest fighting formations. Based in Kaduna, its AOR covers Kaduna, Kano, Jigawa and Katsina. Sokoto, Kebbi and Zamfara align with 8 Division; Niger State with 9 Division under the 2026 expansion.
economy: Defence garrison, barracks infrastructure, and military logistics hub.
climate: Guinea savanna with distinct harmattan season.

name: 2 Division (Ibadan)
summary: Headquarters at Ibadan; responsible for the southwest states outside the Lagos metropolitan command.
description: The 2 Division is the Nigerian Army's southwest-facing formation. Its area of responsibility spans Oyo, Osun, Ekiti and Ondo. Lagos and Ogun are under 81 Division; Kwara under 9 Division (2026 expansion).
economy: Defence garrison and cantonment services for the southwest region.

name: 3 Division (Jos)
summary: Headquarters near Jos; covers Plateau, Bauchi and Gombe after the 2026 divisional expansion.
description: 3 Division operates from the Jos Plateau. Following the July 2026 expansion to twelve divisions, Benue, Nasarawa and Kogi moved to 5 Division, Kwara and Niger to 9 Division, and Taraba and Adamawa to 10 Division. 3 Division now focuses on Plateau, Bauchi and Gombe.
economy: Defence cantonments, peace-support logistics, and Middle Belt garrison network.
climate: Highland climate on the Jos Plateau; warmer southern sectors.

name: 6 Division (Port Harcourt)
summary: Headquarters in Port Harcourt; Niger Delta states under the active division (Rivers, Bayelsa, Delta, Edo).
description: 6 Division is the Nigerian Army's Port Harcourt formation and the lead division for Joint Task Force operations in the Niger Delta. Its active area of responsibility remains Rivers, Bayelsa, Delta and Edo until 83 Division (Benin City) reaches full operational capability; the approved 2026 plan then assigns Edo, Delta and Bayelsa to 83 Division while 6 Division focuses on Rivers.
founded: Created to secure the Niger Delta theatre
economy: Oil-region security, JTF deployments, delta logistics support.
climate: Equatorial; heavy rainfall and mangrove delta.

name: 7 Division (Maiduguri)
summary: Headquarters in Maiduguri; frontline counter-insurgency division for Borno and Yobe.
description: 7 Division was raised specifically for the northeast counter-insurgency theatre. It is the Nigerian Army's principal fighting formation against insurgent groups in Borno, Yobe, and adjoining Lake Chad basin areas, with extensive forward operating bases.
economy: Counter-insurgency garrison, theatre logistics, military-civilian aid coordination.
climate: Sahel; very hot dry season with short rains.

name: 8 Division (Sokoto)
summary: Headquarters in Sokoto; area of responsibility for the far northwest states and Niger border arc.
description: 8 Division is tasked with the far-northwest corridor, covering the Sokoto caliphate heartland and contiguous border states facing Niger. Responsibilities include border defence, anti-banditry operations, and coordination with regional security forces.
founded: Restructured to cover the far northwest frontier and border security corridor
economy: Border security, anti-banditry deployments, caliphate-region garrison.
climate: Sahel; short rains and intense harmattan.

name: 81 Division (Lagos)
summary: Headquarters in Lagos; area of responsibility is Lagos and Ogun states only.
description: 81 Division is the Nigerian Army's Lagos garrison formation, responsible for the Lagos metropolis, Apapa and Lekki ports, and adjoining Ogun State (including the Lagos–Ogun industrial corridor). It provides ceremonial duties and port-sector security.
founded: Lagos garrison restructured as a division-level formation
economy: Lagos garrison, port security forces, state ceremonial duties.

name: 82 Division (Enugu)
summary: Headquarters in Enugu; area of responsibility covers the southeast and eastern south-south states.
description: 82 Division is the Nigerian Army's formation for the southeast. Based in Enugu, it extends across the five southeast states plus the eastern south-south corridor, handling internal security and the Cameroon border flank near Cross River.
founded: Post-civil-war reorganisation for the eastern theatre
economy: Southeast garrison, border security near Cameroon, eastern corridor deployments.
climate: Tropical; escarpment hills and rainforest fringe.

name: Guards Brigade (Abuja)
summary: Headquarters in Abuja; elite formation protecting the FCT, presidential villa, and federal institutions.
description: The Guards Brigade is the Nigerian Army's elite capital-guard formation. It is responsible for protecting the Presidential Villa (Aso Rock), National Assembly, Supreme Court, foreign missions, and the wider Abuja Federal Capital Territory. It also mounts state ceremonial parades.
founded: FCT-era elite brigade for Abuja and federal institutions
economy: FCT defence, federal institutions protection, state ceremonial events.
climate: Guinea savanna with cooler nights than the coast.

name: Nigerian Army Headquarters (Abuja)
summary: Army HQ at Abacha Barracks, Abuja — coordinates all divisions and national land-defence policy.
description: The Nigerian Army Headquarters at Abacha Barracks (Garki, Abuja) is the apex command for land forces. It directs the six divisional headquarters, the Guards Brigade, and specialist corps, and tasks formations across every geopolitical zone.
economy: National defence command, staff colleges liaison, joint operations coordination.
climate: Guinea savanna around the Federal Capital.

name: 10 Division (Jalingo) — new
type: New Nigerian Army divisional headquarters (North-East and North-Central)
summary: New divisional HQ approved July 2026 for Taraba and Adamawa states.
description: 10 Division is a new Nigerian Army divisional headquarters headquartered in Jalingo, Taraba State, created under the expansion to twelve divisions approved on 23 July 2026. It assumes responsibility for Taraba and Adamawa states, absorbing the two states that were previously part of 7 Division (Maiduguri) area of responsibility. Its creation places a divisional headquarters on the road and rail corridor between the Benue Valley and the Mambilla Plateau.
statusDetail: Approved by the President on 23 July 2026 and announced by the Presidency. A General Officer Commanding was appointed on 30 July 2026. It is part of Phase 1 of the new force structure, targeted for completion by September 2026. Formation type has not been publicly disclosed.
mouSigned: Not applicable — a military formation, not a commercial project
mouParties: Federal Government of Nigeria (Presidency and Ministry of Defence); Nigerian Army
mouSignificance: Creation approved by President Bola Ahmed Tinubu on 23 July 2026, announced by Bayo Onanuga. A General Officer Commanding was appointed by the Chief of Army Staff, Lt.-Gen. Waidi Shaibu, on 30 July 2026.

milestones.event: President Tinubu approves creation of the 10 Division headquarters in Jalingo, Taraba State.
Army appoints a General Officer Commanding for 10 Division.
Phase 1 target: division established and operational.

phase: Phase 1 of two (targeted complete by September 2026)
aorNote: Taraba and Adamawa states, separated from the former 7 Division (Maiduguri) area of responsibility.
significance: Brings divisional-level command to the Benue–Mambilla corridor and eases the load on 7 Division in the North-East.

name: 5 Division (Makurdi) — new
summary: New divisional HQ approved July 2026 for Benue, Nasarawa and Kogi states.
description: 5 Division is one of four divisional headquarters created when President Bola Tinubu approved the Nigerian Army's expansion from eight to twelve divisions on 23 July 2026. Headquartered in Makurdi, it takes over responsibility for Benue, Nasarawa and Kogi states from 3 Division and previously uncommitted forces in the North-Central theatre. The Army states that the division will commence operations on attaining Initial Operational Capability and progress towards Full Operational Capability.
statusDetail: Approved by the President on 23 July 2026 and announced by the Presidency. A General Officer Commanding was appointed on 30 July 2026. It forms part of Phase 1 of the new force structure, which the Army expects to complete by September 2026. Operations begin on attaining Initial Operational Capability (IOC), with Full Operational Capability (FOC) to follow.
mouSigned: Not applicable — a military formation, not a commercial project
mouParties: Federal Government of Nigeria (Presidency and Ministry of Defence); Nigerian Army
mouSignificance: Creation approved by President Bola Ahmed Tinubu on 23 July 2026, announced by the President's Special Adviser on Information and Strategy, Bayo Onanuga. The division is commanded by a General Officer Commanding appointed by the Chief of Army Staff, Lt.-Gen. Waidi Shaibu.

milestones.event: President Tinubu approves the expansion of the Nigerian Army from eight to twelve divisions, including a new divisional headquarters in Makurdi.
Benue State Government confirms approval of the 5 Division Headquarters in Makurdi.
Army appoints a General Officer Commanding for 5 Division.
Phase 1 target: 5, 9 and 10 Divisions established and existing formations reorganised.

phase: Phase 1 of two (targeted complete by September 2026)
aorNote: Benue, Nasarawa and Kogi states. Benue, Nasarawa and Kogi are carved out of the former 3 Division (Jos) North-Central area of responsibility.
significance: Restores a dedicated divisional headquarters for the North-Central states and cuts response time for the Benue Valley and Niger-Benue corridor.

name: 83 Division (Benin City) — new
summary: New divisional HQ approved July 2026 for Edo, Delta and Bayelsa states; Phase 2, due December 2026.
description: 83 Division is a new Nigerian Army divisional headquarters headquartered in Benin City, Edo State, created under the expansion to twelve divisions approved on 23 July 2026. It takes over Edo, Delta and Bayelsa states — the bulk of the former 6 Division (Port Harcourt) area of responsibility in the Niger Delta and the Benin Creek corridor. Unlike the other three new divisions, 83 Division falls in the second phase of implementation and is the latest to be established.
statusDetail: Approved by the President on 23 July 2026 and announced by the Presidency. A General Officer Commanding was appointed on 30 July 2026. It is the only new division in Phase 2 of the restructuring, which also covers further reorganisation of existing formations and is expected to conclude by December 2026. It is therefore the least established of the four.
mouSigned: Not applicable — a military formation, not a commercial project
mouParties: Federal Government of Nigeria (Presidency and Ministry of Defence); Nigerian Army
mouSignificance: Creation approved by President Bola Ahmed Tinubu on 23 July 2026, announced by Bayo Onanuga. A General Officer Commanding was appointed by the Chief of Army Staff on 30 July 2026. Army spokesperson Col. Anele said the new divisions will commence operations immediately upon attaining Initial Operational Capability.

milestones.event: President Tinubu approves creation of the 83 Division headquarters in Benin City, Edo State.
Army appoints a General Officer Commanding for 83 Division; operations to begin on attaining IOC.
Phase 2 target: 83 Division established, with further reorganisation of existing formations complete.

phase: Phase 2 of two (targeted complete by December 2026)
aorNote: Edo, Delta and Bayelsa states, covering the Benin Creek and western Niger Delta, separated from 6 Division (Port Harcourt).
significance: Splits the South-South theatre in two and gives the western Niger Delta and Benin Creek a dedicated divisional headquarters.

name: 9 Division (Ilorin) — new
type: New Nigerian Army divisional headquarters (Kwara and Niger)
summary: New divisional HQ approved July 2026 covering Kwara and Niger states.
description: 9 Division is a new Nigerian Army divisional headquarters headquartered in Ilorin, Kwara State, created under the Army's expansion to twelve divisions approved on 23 July 2026. It assumes responsibility for Kwara and Niger states — a band that includes the disputed Niger–Kwara boundary area and the corridor along the Niger River system into the Sahel. The division falls in Phase 1 of the restructuring.
statusDetail: Approved by the President on 23 July 2026 and announced by the Presidency. A General Officer Commanding was appointed on 30 July 2026. It is part of Phase 1 of the new force structure, targeted for completion by September 2026. The Army has not published its formation type or detailed unit composition.
mouSigned: Not applicable — a military formation, not a commercial project
mouParties: Federal Government of Nigeria (Presidency and Ministry of Defence); Nigerian Army
mouSignificance: Creation approved by President Bola Ahmed Tinubu on 23 July 2026, announced by Bayo Onanuga. Local support was expressed by the Ilorin Emirate Descendants Progressive Union. A General Officer Commanding was appointed by the Chief of Army Staff on 30 July 2026.

milestones.event: President Tinubu approves creation of the 9 Division headquarters in Ilorin, Kwara State.
Ilorin Emirate Descendants Progressive Union publicly welcomes the new division.
Army appoints a General Officer Commanding for 9 Division.
Phase 1 target: division established and operational.

phase: Phase 1 of two (targeted complete by September 2026)
aorNote: Kwara and Niger states, covering the Niger–Kwara belt and the middle Niger corridor.
significance: Fills a divisional gap in the middle belt, improving command coverage for Kwara and Niger states.

name: Central Naval Command (Yenagoa / Warri)
summary: Headquarters of the Nigerian Navy Central Naval Command; responsible for the Niger Delta maritime flank and delta creeks.
description: The Central Naval Command is the Nigerian Navy's delta-facing formation, operating across the Niger Delta creeks from the Escravos/Forcados terminals to Bonny and the central delta waterways. It coordinates JTF maritime components, anti-piracy, and oil-and-gas infrastructure protection.
economy: Delta maritime security, anti-piracy patrols, oil infrastructure defence.
significance: Niger Delta maritime domain and oil-terminal security command.

name: Eastern Naval Command (Calabar)
summary: Headquarters of the Nigerian Navy Eastern Naval Command; covers the Cross River estuary, eastern seaboard, and Cameroon border maritime approaches.
description: The Eastern Naval Command is the Nigerian Navy's formation for the eastern coast, including the Cross River estuary at Calabar, Akwa Ibom coast, and the Bakassi/Cameroon maritime frontier. It supports Calabar Port security and joint border maritime operations.
economy: Eastern seaboard maritime security, Calabar port defence, Cameroon border patrol.
significance: Defence of the eastern coast, Cross River estuary, and Calabar harbour.

name: Western Naval Command (Lagos)
summary: Headquarters of the Nigerian Navy Western Naval Command; controls the Lagos barrier coast and adjoining maritime area.
description: The Western Naval Command is one of the Nigerian Navy's three principal formations, based in the Lagos area with responsibility for the entire western maritime flank including the Lagos Lagoon, Lekki approaches, and Badagry creeks. It hosts key naval bases, jetties, and security assets for the nation's premier port cluster.
economy: Maritime security, naval base infrastructure, coastal patrol.
significance: Defence of Lagos ports, maritime domain awareness, western coast security.

name: Air Training Command (Kaduna)
summary: NAF Air Training Command in Kaduna; runs flying schools, ground-training colleges, and the NAF military aviation pipeline.
description: The Air Training Command (ATC) headquartered at Kaduna (NAF Base Kaduna) is the NAF's training command. It runs the Nigerian Air Force Academy, 301 Flying Training School, 303/325 training wings, and technical schools for pilots, engineers, air defence, and ground-support trades.
founded: Training command evolved with the expansion of the NAF in the 1970s–80s
economy: Flying instruction, maintenance training, cadet academies, and NAF education services.
climate: Guinea savanna with distinct harmattan season.

name: Logistics Command (Ikeja / Lagos)
type: Maintenance, supply, and depot logistics command
summary: NAF Logistics Command at Ikeja (Lagos); manages airframe/engine maintenance depots, supply chains, and national-level NAF logistics support.
description: The Logistics Command (LC) headquartered at NAF Base Ikeja (adjacent to Murtala Muhammed International Airport) is the NAF's maintenance-and-supply backbone. It runs the 431 Engineering Group (airframe depot), 435 Maintenance Depot, national supply and ammunition pipelines, and Lagos-area NAF air-transport detachments.
founded: Logistics Command was created to consolidate NAF maintenance & supply
economy: Aircraft maintenance, engine overhaul, supply depots, ordnance, and NAF logistics services.
climate: Tropical monsoon; high humidity and two rainfall peaks.

name: Mobility Command (Yenagoa / Bayelsa)
type: Airlift, maritime patrol, and special-ops mobility command
summary: NAF Mobility Command HQ in the Yenagoa/Port Harcourt axis; runs transport, SAR, and maritime-patrol fixed-wing and rotary assets.
description: Mobility Command (MC) was stood up to unify the NAF's airlift, search-and-rescue (SAR), and maritime domain-awareness fleets. It operates C-130, Dornier 228, King Air, AW109/139 helicopters, and the ATR-42/72 maritime-patrol fleet, with responsibility over the Niger Delta waterways and coastal approaches.
founded: Established to coordinate NAF mobility & maritime assets
economy: Airlift, maritime patrol, medevac, special-forces insertion, coastal SAR.
climate: Equatorial delta; mangrove wetlands, heavy rainfall.

name: Tactical Air Command (Makurdi)
type: Tactical Air Command HQ — combat & close air support
summary: NAF Tactical Air Command HQ at Makurdi; leads fighter, ground-attack, and helicopter combat elements for northeast and Middle Belt theatres.
description: The Tactical Air Command (TAC) is the NAF's principal fighting headquarters. Based in Makurdi, Benue State, it controls fighter jets (F-7, Alpha Jet, Super Tucano), attack helicopters, and close air support squadrons that have been heavily used in the northeast counter-insurgency campaign and across Middle Belt internal-security deployments.
founded: NAF Makurdi developed as the tactical fighter hub
economy: Combat air operations, maintenance depots, ordnance, and airbase support services.
climate: Guinea savanna; Benue River valley humidity.

name: Nigerian Air Force HQ (Abuja)
type: NAF Headquarters & Abuja air defence sector
summary: Headquarters of the Nigerian Air Force in Abuja; coordinates national air defence, air operations, and the NAF chain of command.
description: The Nigerian Air Force (NAF) is commanded from its headquarters in the Abuja military cantonment area. It oversees air combat, airlift, intelligence, surveillance, and reconnaissance (ISR) across all tactical commands. HQ NAF coordinates with the Defence Headquarters and service branches on joint operations.
founded: Established 1964; HQ relocated to Abuja after FCT became seat of government
economy: HQ staff, defence planning, ISR coordination, and joint task-force liaison.
climate: Guinea savanna; cooler nights than coastal Nigeria.
landmarks: Nnamdi Azikiwe International Airport NAF detachment
